title: Traffic
events_chronological: Tijuana police officers Javier Rodriguez and Manolo Sanchez intercept a drug shipment in the desert and have it taken off them by General Salazar's men.
Salazar recruits Javier onto his anti-cartel task force, which is in fact a front for the Juarez cartel.
Javier helps capture the Obregon cartel's enforcer Francisco Flores, who is tortured into naming the hit man Frankie Flowers.
In San Diego, DEA agents Montel Gordon and Ray Castro arrest the mid-level dealer Eduardo Ruiz and turn him into a witness.
Ruiz's testimony brings the arrest of the importer Carlos Ayala in front of his pregnant wife Helena, who knows nothing about the business.
Ohio judge Robert Wakefield is appointed the President's drug czar and briefed in Washington on a war nobody there thinks can be won.
Wakefield's sixteen-year-old daughter Caroline and her friends free-base at a party, and one of them nearly dies of it.
Helena discovers that the family is bankrupt and that the cartel is threatening her son over her husband's debts.
Helena goes to Carlos's lawyer Arnie Metzger and then arranges a meeting with the Obregon brothers herself.
Caroline's habit moves from cocaine to heroin, and she is arrested and thrown out of school.
Helena commissions Frankie Flowers to kill Ruiz before he can testify.
Wakefield tours the border, meets Salazar, and is told by everyone he talks to that treatment is the only thing that works.
Caroline runs away and starts prostituting herself for drugs in an inner-city motel.
Frankie Flowers's car bomb kills Ray Castro instead of Ruiz.
Wakefield abandons his Washington duties and searches the motels of Cincinnati for his daughter himself.
Manolo tries to sell what he knows about Salazar to the DEA and is executed in the desert in front of Javier.
Frankie Flowers poisons Ruiz in protective custody, and the case against Carlos Ayala collapses.
Javier gives Salazar up to the DEA, and the general is exposed as the Juarez cartel's man and arrested.
Wakefield resigns at his own press conference, saying he cannot fight a war against his own family.
Gordon plants a bug at the party celebrating Carlos's release, Helena takes over running the business, and Javier watches the floodlit baseball game he asked for as his price.
syuzhet_notes: Three strands - Tijuana, Washington and Ohio, San Diego - are intercut from the first reel and told apart by colour rather than captions, with Mexico bleached yellow and Ohio filtered cold blue. The strands run concurrently, so most of the reordering here is lateral, the film moving between cities at roughly the same date; the exceptions are told-order bullets 6, 7 and 11, which drop back behind their neighbours to fill in what a character already knew.
fabula_notes: The three strands never fully converge and share almost no scenes, so the ordering across them is inferred from a handful of common markers - Ruiz's arrest, his testimony, his death. Carlos Ayala's business dealings before his arrest are established through testimony and never dramatised.
